Claire (AE): Quick heads up — QuantumHealth security team just sent over a networking checklist for the Private deployment. They want confirmation on our recommended egress architecture and a concise firewall allowlist before we finalize pricing. Thread to coordinate.

Ravi (NetOps): What are the specific asks?

Lee (Solutions Eng): TL;DR from the checklist they sent: (1) static egress IP(s) for outbound model/telemetry calls; (2) TLS inspection compatibility / SNI passthrough guidance; (3) option for zero direct internet egress (all traffic via customer proxy); (4) required ports and CIDR allowlist; and (5) whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is the recommended path for a Private deployment.

Claire (AE): Pricing note — if they require Dedicated capacity + guaranteed static egress IPs we likely need a Reserved Dedicated plan + managed NAT/EIP which will affect the monthly commit. @Ben (RevOps) FYI.

Ravi (NetOps): Short technical answers: PrivateLink is primarily for inbound (customer -> our endpoint). Outbound egress from our compute will follow whatever NAT/proxy exists in whichever VPC the workers run in. If QuantumHealth wants zero outbound internet, we can run workers inside their VPC (Private deployment) with no internet route; in that case model pulls must be staged inside the VPC or we need a secure pull via their proxy. We support TLS passthrough (SNI) — full TLS inspection (MITM) will break mTLS and some cert pinning unless they delegate certs or we terminate TLS in their proxy.

Lee (Solutions Eng): Draft firewall snippet for them to whitelist/control-plane connectivity (examples only):
```
# Control plane endpoints (allow outbound from customer admin to control plane)
34.89.12.100/32  TCP  443  control-plane.redwood.com
34.89.12.101/32  TCP  443  control-plane.redwood.com
# Model/artifact pulls (optional; better to mirror into VPC)
52.14.200.0/24  TCP  443  models-cache.redwood.com
```
If they want model downloads blocked to internet entirely, we need an S3/VPC mirror or an allowlist to a private bucket.

Claire (AE): QuantumHealth also asked whether PrivateLink can be used so our service egresses via their network for 3rd party calls (short answer?).

Ravi (NetOps): PrivateLink doesn't change outbound behavior from our compute — it gives you a private endpoint into our service. Outbound egress still needs NAT in the VPC where compute runs. Options: (A) run compute in their VPC (no outbound), (B) run in our infra but route outbound through their proxy via a VPN/partner link (complex), or (C) allow managed static egress IPs from our side and let their firewall accept those IPs. Note on TLS inspection: recommend SNI allowlist on corporate proxy instead of MITM whenever possible to preserve end-to-end cert properties.

Sven (Security): Couple of security Qs to include in reply: do they require customer HSM for keys or are KMS-managed keys acceptable? Who owns TLS certs for inbound endpoints? Also ask for acceptable cipher suites and whether they enforce mTLS.

Ben (RevOps): Ballpark on pricing uplift: if they require Dedicated + static egress IP(s) + managed NAT we usually add ~+30% on top of the Dedicated baseline to cover reserved egress capacity and IP management. Will confirm exact figures after infrastructure sign-off.

Lee (Solutions Eng): I'll draft a one-page network diagram + a minimal allowlist and a split-tunnel recommendation. Quick question to @Alex (QuantumHealth NetOps): do you run corporate TLS inspection appliances (e.g., Zscaler/Bluecoat) that replace certs, or do you only use SNI/network proxy? That affects whether we can rely on TLS passthrough.

Alex (QuantumHealth NetOps): We run Zscaler TLS inspection for most egress and require outbound through corporate proxy. We prefer not to replace certs on the app side. Can you provide a concise IP list and a recommended split-tunnel config? Also what is the smallest port list you need?

Claire (AE): Thanks Alex — we'll send a 1-pager + allowlist and a split-tunnel example. Draft will include: minimal ports, control plane IPs, model pull options, and the two deployment patterns (workers in your VPC vs. managed static egress). Expect a draft by EOD PST. :thumbsup:
